note:
Regenerated 2026-08-17 (eighth pass) after the tier-calibration task fixed four measurement mechanisms in ext/DesignTool -- the module was renamed from LayoutTool the same day, and styles/layouts/ was rebuilt, so the seventh-pass baseline described neither the tier nor the site any more. Full record with the numbers: ai/2026-08-17/tier-calibration/; the evidence that convicted the tier: ai/2026-08-17/vision-baseline/. WHAT CHANGED IN THE MEASUREMENTS, mechanisms only -- not one threshold in taste/ranges.js was touched: (1) `width-used` is now ONE implementation shared with score.metrics(), and it measures COVERAGE (the union of the intervals content occupies) rather than a SPAN from the leftmost content box to the rightmost, clipped to the frame. The span assumed what it was measuring -- that what lies between the two edges is continuous -- so a topbar with a logo left and an avatar right read 100%; taste tried to escape that by banding leaves into 24px rows and taking the median, which on every page with a nav rail measured THE RAIL (6-10% on 17 of 18 corpus pages against an `ok` floor of 0.28, a hard zero forfeiting 13% of the tier's weight uniformly), while score.js's span read 208% and 149% on two pages whose `
` scrolls a 2640px code line sideways. (2) The six bands whose subject is the page's CONTENT -- measure, contrast, repetition, slivers, depth, lanes -- now read inside ratios.region() instead of the whole app shell; `depth` is measured relative to that region. (3) `repetition` requires a group's siblings to share a CLASS, which its own wording in ranges.js has always said and the implementation never did: probe.label() returns the bare tag for an unclassed element, so twenty sibling 
 in a markdown block counted as one repeated component and every article on the site read as a wall. (4) polish.js's `heading-offset` pairs a heading with its next block SIBLING and measures to the leftmost drawn box inside it, instead of taking whatever text node came next in a global y-sort; the 96px "deliberate indent" escape is gone, because it only ever existed to survive the wrong pairing. `bands` is 11 [value, credit] pairs in taste/ranges.js RANGES order, each rounded to 2 decimals -- zip with RANGES for id/weight/why, nothing here duplicates them. `counts` REPLACES the old `analyze` field: findings.json no longer has an aggregate score to store, so a row carries the finding census instead. `ignored` is the share of the root's area probe.IGNORE skipped; `mostly_picture` is true at ignored >= 0.5. `score` can be null (nothing measurable) -- a null score is unrated, not zero, and `grade` is a dash in that case; rank readers must skip null scores, not sort them last. `tier` is sha256[0:16] of probe.js + ratios.js + rules.js + polish.js + score.js + taste/{read,ranges,taste}.js -- ratios.js and polish.js were ADDED to the fingerprint by this pass, because width_used lives in one and heading-offset in the other and the tier could previously move without the hash moving. Verification before this pass: tests/ 23/23 declared verdicts pass at 400/1280/1920/3440, and taste/corpus/ reads 27 agree / 1 disagree / 14 n/a with the `pinned the body narrow` case now agreeing on all seven subjects at a full -1 credit (it previously read n/a on `gallery` because that subject already scored zero on the broken band). ⚠ `tier` was RECOMPUTED after the rows were measured, from 0b1c00b52df132f2 to f1a010f3193c8b0c: the only change to any fingerprinted file after the sweep was a COMMENT trimmed out of ratios.js (its long-form rationale moved to knowledge/ideal-ranges.md, per RULE#9/#10), so no row was re-measured and none needed to be. A hash that is knowingly stale is worse than one that is explained — but if you find this clause on a future pass, the honest reading is that a fingerprint recomputed by hand is one someone could have got wrong.
